# Implementation Plan: crews-mail-delivery-via-codex-injection

<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-mail-delivery-via-codex-injection"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-12. Planning-only handoff: this plan spans two repos and must not be driven as one blind `/implement-with-ralph` run.*

## Overview

This task removes the listener-subprocess dependency for **codex members** while preserving the `.crews` mailbox and review cursor as the only source of truth. The chosen v1 design keeps the durable mailbox model intact, adds a tiny **crews-side MCP wake producer** on mailbox writes, and adds a **general Codex notification-to-next-turn wake primitive** that turns one allowlisted server notification into one queued next-turn prompt.

The wake is advisory only. It never marks mail reviewed, never advances `lastReviewedSeq`, and never replaces `review-mail` / `markReviewed` as the ack path. Claude and Copilot keep the current listener model unchanged. Because the work spans the `codex\` submodule and `ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\`, the implementation must be split into repo-specific jobs with an explicit ordering for the codex-only gate relaxation and live dogfood.

### Technical Constraints
- No MCP protocol change is required. The missing work is implementation-only: a crews MCP server and a native Codex consumer that turns an allowlisted MCP notification into queued next-turn input.
- **General-vs-crews-specific decision:** the Codex consumer should be a **general wake primitive** keyed by `{ serverName, notificationKind }`, with crews as the first registered route. The primitive must not hard-code crews mailbox semantics into the queueing seam itself.
- **Option decision:** choose **Option B (`notifications/message`) for v1**.
  - Why: it satisfies the "minimal codex-fork seam" mandate, needs no `resources/subscribe` client plumbing, and still preserves the wake-hint-only contract because the mailbox remains authoritative.
  - Deferred migration path: the same general Codex primitive can later accept `ResourceUpdated` once Codex grows typed `resources/subscribe` support and crews decides the mailbox URI is worth modeling.
- **v1 scope decision:** start with **codex members only**, not codex leads. Current lead runtime is Copilot, codex leads are a follow-up, and listenerless lead behavior is a larger operational surface.
- **Codex fork discipline:** every unavoidable upstream-canonical edit must carry `// SANDBOX PATCH:` markers and add/update `codex\docs\implementation\patch-surface.md` section 14 (invariant mapping) and section 15 (replant note). Prefer overlay-first packaging for new logic.

## Approach

### Architecture

#### 1. Crews-side producer (v1 = Option B)
Add a small **Node.js stdio MCP server** at the plugin root and wire it through `.codex-plugin\plugin.json` via `"mcpServers": "./.mcp.codex.json"`. The server's job is intentionally narrow:
- after MCP initialization completes, write a per-actor **ready stamp** (for example `codex-wake-bridge.json`) containing `{ sessionId, actorName, crew, mode }`; hooks use this as the capability proof that the bridge is actually alive for the current session;
- perform exactly one **startup catch-up** after that ready stamp is written if `lastReviewRequiredSeq > lastReviewedSeq`;
- watch the actor directory (`mailbox.json` plus the manifest/review cursor state) and emit `notifications/message` wakes when unread state advances;
- dedupe wakes so v1 guarantees one outstanding wake per unread generation keyed by `lastReviewRequiredSeq` rather than one prompt per filesystem event;
- include structured identity data in the notification payload (`actorName`, `crew`, `cwd`) even though v1 only queues a generic wake hint, so a future Option-A mailbox URI route does not require a payload-format break;
- never read or mutate `lastReviewedSeq` except for read-only comparisons.

`appendMailboxWithSender(...)` remains the single durable write chokepoint, but it does not talk directly to the MCP server. The server learns about new mail by watching the same durable state the rest of crews already treats as source-of-truth.

The wake payload should be minimal, for example: `[crews] pending mailbox update; run review-mail to drain`. The body stays out of the wake.

Lock the v1 producer/consumer contract up front so the repos can develop in parallel without drifting:
- `serverName = "crews"`
- `notificationKind = "logging_message"`
- notification payload carries `{ actorName, crew, cwd }`
- synthesized prompt text is the fixed codex-member action hint `[crews] pending mailbox update; run review-mail to drain`

#### 2. Codex-side general wake primitive
Extend the existing overlay crate `codex\codex-rs-overlay\codex-mcp-notification-bridge\` with a consumer module that owns:
- allowlist matching on `{ serverName, notificationKind }`;
- prompt synthesis for the next-turn wake item;
- a tiny API that hands a synthesized `ResponseInputItem` back to the session layer.

Then add a small upstream-canonical seam in the existing session event flow so an allowlisted `EventMsg::McpServerNotification` can:
1. synthesize one next-turn prompt,
2. call `queue_response_items_for_next_turn(...)`,
3. call `request_pending_work_wake()`.

The call site is intentionally **not** `realtime_text_for_event()`. That function is the UI-text sink, not the owner of queue-side effects. The consumer belongs in the session event-dispatch path, reusing the exact queue-then-wake pattern already used in `async_watcher.rs:166-189`.

**Seams considered**

| Option | Placement | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Happy CLI only (`packages\happy-cli\src\codex\mcpNotificationConsumer.ts` pattern) | Rejected | Solves only Happy-wrapped Codex, not plain crews-spawned codex members. |
| B | Extend `codex-mcp-notification-bridge` with a consumer module plus 1-3 line session seam | **Chosen** | Best match for Codex tenant 1: overlay-first, small canonical touchpoints, reusable general primitive, and no redundant second crate beside the existing Stage-A bridge. |
| C | Inline `turn.rs` ownership of matching + prompt synthesis | Rejected | Higher upstream churn in a central file and worse rebase surface. |

**Edit-budget estimate:** ~40-70 LoC of upstream-canonical Rust plus ~120-200 LoC in overlay code/tests/docs.  
**Re-conflict probability:** medium-low, provided the canonical seam stays additive and patch-surface registration is updated in the same ship.

#### 3. Capability proof and launch-time enablement
Relaxing listener-arm gates must be based on a proof that the bridge is active for the **current session**, not on `manifest.engine === 'codex'` alone.

Use a two-part proof:
- `hooks\actors.js` stamps the codex launcher with `-c features.mcp_server_notifications=true` so the session can actually receive the bridged events;
- the new crews MCP server writes a session-scoped ready stamp after MCP initialization succeeds. PreToolUse / Stop / briefing code should trust the bridge only when that stamp exists and its `sessionId` matches the current actor manifest.

This avoids a false-positive relax-on-launch-intent path. If the server never comes up, the ready stamp never appears and codex keeps the current listener model.

#### 4. Codex-only reachability relaxation
Once the explicit capability flag is present:
- `pre-tool-use.js` should no longer force listener-arm-first for codex members; if unread mail exists it should still prefer `review-mail`, but it must stop telling codex members to arm a listener after every wake.
- `stop.js` should stop requiring an armed listener for codex members with the bridge enabled.
- `review-required` and strict-ack semantics stay unchanged: pending mail still blocks until drained; the wake is not an ack.
- Claude and Copilot branches remain byte-intent unchanged.

### Implementation Strategy
1. Build the **Codex general wake primitive** and its patch-surface / invariant-test scaffolding.
2. Build the **crews MCP producer**, ready-stamp capability proof, and startup catch-up after MCP initialization, but keep listener gates unchanged while the bridge is not yet declared active.
3. Add the **actors.js launch-time feature enablement** and codex-only gate / briefing relaxation.
4. Dogfood through the **installed Codex path**, not just source trees:
   - `copilot plugin update` is insufficient for codex members;
   - ensure the codex marketplace points at the toolkit checkout (`codex plugin marketplace add D:\harness-efforts\codexu\ai-developer-toolkit` if needed);
   - refresh the codex-side plugin cache with `codex plugin add crews@ai-developer-toolkit`;
   - then spawn a codex member and verify mailbox-write wake -> review-mail drain -> no listener requirement.

## Scope

### In Scope
- V1 producer choice: `notifications/message`.
- General Codex next-turn wake primitive with a code-owned allowlist; first route is `{ server: "crews", kind: "logging_message" }`.
- Crews mailbox-write wake emission via a watched durable-state producer plus one post-initialize startup catch-up.
- Ready-stamp capability proof, actors.js launch-time feature enablement, and codex-only listener-gate / briefing relaxation.
- Codex patch-surface documentation, invariant tests/guards, and installed-path dogfood.
- Clear dual-repo handoff and ordering for the lead.

### Out of Scope
- `resources/subscribe` client plumbing and `notifications/resources/updated` for v1.
- `sampling/createMessage` reply-path support.
- Claude or Copilot listenerless delivery.
- Codex lead listenerless delivery.
- Replacing `.crews` mailbox history as the source of truth.
- Treating a wake prompt as acknowledgement or cursor advancement.

## Risk Areas

| Risk | Why it matters | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Logging-notification semantics are weaker than resource-updated | The wake does not identify a mailbox URI and cannot rely on a subscribe contract | Keep the consumer general and route-based so Option A can replace only the producer/route later without a second queue bridge patch. |
| Gate relaxation could silently punch a hole for codex sessions that do not actually have the bridge | `manifest.engine === "codex"` alone is too weak | Require a current-session ready-stamp capability proof; absent or stale stamp keeps the current listener behavior. |
| Codex seam lands in the wrong place and grows upstream conflict surface | Central Rust files are high-churn rebase hotspots | Overlay-first helper, additive canonical seam, and same-ship patch-surface / invariant updates. |
| Wake path accidentally mutates review state | That would split truth between transcript and mailbox | Keep all review cursor writes in `review-mail` / `markReviewed` only; add tests that wake paths do not touch `lastReviewedSeq`. |
| Installed codex members still run an old crews plugin | Codex uses a separate plugin cache from Copilot CLI | Make codex-cache refresh part of the dogfood AC; do not treat `copilot plugin update` as sufficient. |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `crews` allowlisted `logging_message` notification can enqueue exactly one next-turn wake prompt in raw codex and call `request_pending_work_wake()`.
- [ ] Non-allowlisted notifications and `Feature::McpServerNotifications == false` remain event-only/no-op paths.
- [ ] The queue-side consumer is invoked from the session event-dispatch path, not from `realtime_text_for_event()`.
- [ ] The crews MCP server writes a current-session ready stamp after MCP initialization and emits one startup catch-up wake only after that ready stamp exists.
- [ ] Crews emits one deduped wake per unread generation after durable mailbox state advances.
- [ ] Wake delivery never changes `lastReviewedSeq` / `lastReviewedAt`; only `review-mail` / `markReviewed` advance review state.
- [ ] Codex members with a ready-stamp capability proof no longer require an armed listener in PreToolUse or Stop, while Claude/Copilot behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Review-required and strict-ack semantics remain mailbox-driven and unchanged by the new wake path.
- [ ] Codex fork edits are patch-surface registered with `// SANDBOX PATCH:` markers, a section-14 invariant mapping, and a section-15 replant note.
- [ ] Crews version and marketplace stamps are bumped through `scripts\bump-version.js`, and `tests\version.test.js` is updated in the same ship.
- [ ] Installed-path dogfood proves the end-to-end member flow: mailbox write -> codex wake prompt -> `review-mail` drain -> no listener requirement.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

## US-001: Add the general Codex wake-notification consumer
**Repo:** `codex\`

**Description:** As a codex member runtime, I want one allowlisted MCP server notification to become one queued next-turn wake prompt so that raw codex sessions can react to crews mail without a listener subprocess.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] The v1 allowlist route `{ server: "crews", kind: "logging_message" }` queues one next-turn prompt and wakes pending work.
- [ ] Feature-off and non-allowlisted notifications remain inert.
- [ ] The consumer seam is called from the session event-dispatch flow, not from `realtime_text_for_event()`.
- [ ] The canonical seam is overlay-first with minimal upstream-canonical edits, and patch-surface docs/tests are updated.
- [ ] Typecheck passes for the affected Codex crates.

**Dependencies:** None  
**Estimated complexity:** large

## US-002: Add the crews Codex MCP wake producer and startup catch-up
**Repo:** `ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\`

**Description:** As a codex crews member, I want durable mailbox state changes to produce a deduped wake hint so that codex can prompt me to drain my mailbox without a listener subprocess.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] The Codex plugin manifest sets `"mcpServers": "./.mcp.codex.json"`, and the plugin-root `.mcp.codex.json` launches a Node.js stdio MCP server through a stable entrypoint.
- [ ] The MCP server watches the actor's durable mailbox/manifest state; hooks do not attempt direct IPC into the server process.
- [ ] Successful unread-state advances emit a deduped `notifications/message` wake.
- [ ] The MCP server writes a current-session ready stamp and performs startup catch-up only after MCP initialization succeeds.
- [ ] The notification payload carries structured identity data for future Option-A migration.
- [ ] The wake producer never marks mail reviewed or drains the mailbox.

**Dependencies:** None  
**Estimated complexity:** medium

## US-003: Relax codex-only listener gates behind an explicit bridge capability and dogfood the installed flow
**Repo:** `ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\`

**Description:** As a codex crews member, I want the hooks and briefings to treat the MCP wake bridge as my reachability mechanism so that I no longer have to arm a listener after every wake.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `hooks\actors.js` enables `features.mcp_server_notifications=true` on the codex launcher path and participates in the bridge-proof contract.
- [ ] PreToolUse and Stop branch on the ready-stamp capability proof, not on engine alone.
- [ ] Codex members with the flag stop receiving listener-arm requirements; codex members without it keep the old behavior.
- [ ] Review-required / strict-ack behavior stays unchanged.
- [ ] The installed codex plugin cache is refreshed and a live codex-member dogfood passes end-to-end.

**Dependencies:** US-001, US-002  
**Estimated complexity:** medium
